To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
dynamic collimator optimization is an efficient and practical approach to improve target coverage and reduce normal tissue dose in stereotactic radio-surgery and stereotactic body radiotherapy.

(i) the use of a fixed collimator angle during arc-based stereotatic radiotherapy is associated with a significant increase in the number of high dose regions, and (ii) the use of an optimized dynamic collimator during arc-based stereoradotherapy is able to reduce the number of high-dose regions, without compromising dose conformity and target volume coverage.

(1) dynamic collimator rotation (DCR) is superior to fixed collimator angle (FCA) in arc-based stereostatic radiotherapy for the majority of the brain tumors; and (2) DCR can improve the dose distribution for brain tumor patients with irregularly shaped tumors and/or with a large distance between the target and the brainstem, compared with conventional FCA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation of an automatic collimator optimization method for stereotactic radio-surgery.
the development and evaluation of the dynamic collimator optimization method for arc-based stereotaxic radiotherapy, with the aim of improving target conformity and sparing of critical organs.
the use of the dynamic collimator technique in the optimization of arc-based stereotatic radiotherapy (SRT) plans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the absence of clinical data to support the superiority of one technique over another, the choice of the best technique for the delivery of stereotactic radio-surgery depends on the availability of the different technologies, on the expertise of the staff and on the clinical indications.

the dynamic collimator angle optimization (DCO) is a promising approach in stereotactic radio-surgery (SRS), and it is a good alternative to fixed collimator angle optimization for the treatment of brain tumors with a small volume and a steep dose gradient.

the dynamic collimator optimization is a better choice for stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS), while the fixed collimator optimization is preferred for stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) due to the different dose distributions.
